options: Patch spawn_verifier to surface returncode/stderr so a blocked spawn is loud rather than NO_VERDICT — fixes the fail-open regardless of the permission question
Add a Bash permission rule allowing the nested verifier spawn, accepting that verify runs a --dangerously-skip-permissions subagent

status: resolved:Premise was WRONG. tessera-verify is not blocked from inside a session — it now runs and returns CONFIRMED with positive controls. The direct 'claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions' I ran by hand was blocked, and I wrongly generalized that to the tool's own spawn; the NO_VERDICTs were transient. The real defect was option 1, now fixed: spawn_verifier discarded returncode/stderr, so a failed spawn became NO_VERDICT, and scripts/verify/scan.py counted that event as dispositioning verification — a verifier that never ran silenced the Stop-hook backstop. Fixed at all three layers (raise VerifierDidNotRun, exit 2 + spawn_error in the event, scan.py ignores spawn_error events) plus raw_excerpt so NO_VERDICT is diagnosable. Options 2 and 3 are moot.
